newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
More than 210 Tamil separatists (LTTE) killed and over 300 wounded in Tuesday's attack launched by rebels to destroy divisional headquarters directing Operation Jaya Sikuru, militay sources said.

Leader of main opposition United National Party (UNP) Ranil Wickremesinghe, to make statement soon on his party's boycott of government-owned Lake House newspapers. The UNP is boycotting Lake House papers, alleging that they do not give a balanced coverage.
Government forces regain control of Thandikulam and Nochchimoddai, which fell temporarily into the hands of the LTTE, in massive twin strikes launched by them on Tuesday.
A total of 387 security service personnel injured in recent clashes between troops and LTTE, rushed to Anuradhapura and Colombo hospitals, sources say.
A total of 110 security personnel and 210 LTTE rebels killed in attacks at Thandikulam and Nochchimoddai, security sources say.
Police detect press used to print forged currency notes in Nuwara Eliya, in central Sri Lanka.
Five medical personnel attached to the Army and stationed at Thandikulam, abducted by LTTE, sources say.

New transport minister A.H.M. Fowzie moves to get tyres for 200 government buses which were off the road due to a lack of tyres. Former minister Srimanee Athulathmudali was sacked by President Kumaratunga in a cabinet reshuffle on Monday.
